title: ENetConnection not being correctly disposed when disconnecting server as host, only happens on C#
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot v4.3.stable.mono.official

### Issue description

Garbage collector not correctly disposing the current **ENetConnection** when using **ENetMultiplayerPeer** as server, the used port to create the server remains occupied until the end of the application, when it gets reclaimed by the **OS**.

What I expect to, is to the garbage collector to properly dispose the peer and connection after setting ```Multiplayer.MultiplayerPeer = null```. This is the way that the [High-Level multiplayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/networking/high_level_multiplayer.html) doc. page show us to terminate networking, I tested it using GDScript and it works fine, but it doesn't works when using C#, I suspect is an error in the way the ```Dispose()``` method is implemented in either ENetMultiplayerPeer or ENetConnection.

The only workaround I found that doesn't involve killing the program is calling `Destroy()` in the underlying **ENetConnection** inside **ENetMultiplayerPeer**, basically ```peer.Host.Destroy()```, but sometimes the garbage collector will complain with an error that the current **host** is **null** after setting ```Multiplayer.MultiplayerPeer = null```, I included an UI and this workaround in the MRP.

### Steps to reproduce

-Create new Project.
-Create script Lobby.cs
-Copy the C# **Example lobby implementation** code from [High-Level multiplayer doc. page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/networking/high_level_multiplayer.html) to Lobby.cs
-Make Lobby.cs an Autoload.
-override ```_Ready()``` method with:
```c#
public override void _Ready(){
    CreateGame();
    RemoveMultiplayerPeer();
    CreateGame();
}
```
-Build and Run the project.

The second time we call ```CreateGame()``` the debugger will tell us that the "host" after calling ```peer.CreateServer(port, MaxConnections)``` is null, if we call `Debug.WriteLine(CreateGame())` the error returned by ```CreateGame()``` will show us the "**CANT_CREATE**" error.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[csharp_enet_host_server_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18789534/csharp_enet_host_server_bug.zip)
